summary: temper guard's suffix-only path match blocks unrelated files sharing a filename suffix (e.g. .temper/memory/CLAUDE.md), not just true projections

edit.description: path_matches (~782) does a raw string-suffix compare (`file_path.ends_with(candidate_str)`) against each declared projection's `source_path`; a root-level single-segment target (`CLAUDE.md`) suffix-matches ANY path ending in that filename, e.g. the memory kind's authored source `.temper/memory/CLAUDE.md`. Require the match land on a path-segment boundary — the byte before the matched suffix, if any, must be `/` — so a bare string suffix never binds. Both call sites (`matches_projection`, `manifest_write_findings`) share the one helper, so one fix covers both.
Add a regression case: guard fed a payload targeting `.temper/memory/CLAUDE.md` (a path that merely ends in a projected file's name, not the projection itself) resolves Allow, not Block/Warn/Note.

tests.asserts: a file_path ending in a projected file's bare name but naming an unrelated path (no path-segment boundary) resolves GuardVerdict::Allow

acceptance: This repo's own reproduction (`echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":".../.temper/memory/CLAUDE.md"}}' | temper guard .`) exits 0, not 2; the new tests/install.rs case pins it.
notes: Field report (cascade adoption, engine 0.0.15, observed 2026-08-10, inbox): the memory kind's projection source_path is the single-segment root file "CLAUDE.md"; path_matches' naive ends_with binds any path sharing that filename suffix, not just a real projection. scoped at f240dc35

summary: check cannot resolve a mention target addressing a host-scoped embedded leaf, so it dangles at check though emit already validates the same address

edit.description: node_from_address (~1044) parses every mention target as `kind:name` (split on the first `:`); a target shaped `<host-member>/<kind>/<key>/<child-path>` (the embedded-leaf grammar `embeddedLeafMentionRows` in sdk/src/declarations.ts already authors for a mention's member/source side) has no `:`, so it falls into the bare-requirement branch and edge_resolves (~1075) reports it dangling against the roster instead of resolving it against the embedded corpus. Give route_mentions/edge_resolves a path that recognizes the `/`-shaped embedded grammar and resolves it the way read.rs's parse_leaf_address/resolve_leaf already do for leaf-grain narration — share that parser rather than re-deriving it.

parse_leaf_address/resolve_leaf/ParsedLeaf (~801-851) are private to this module; widen visibility (or extract to a shared home) so graph.rs's mention-target resolution reuses the same embedded-leaf address grammar and lookup instead of re-parsing it.

Regression: a lock declaring a nested_member row (embedded leaf) plus a mention whose target addresses that leaf's `<host>/<kind>/<key>/<child-path>` — check must resolve it clean, not report graph.route.

tests.asserts: a mention targeting a real embedded leaf's host-scoped address resolves clean at check; a bogus key still dangles

acceptance: check on a harness whose mention targets a real embedded leaf (the exact `<host>/<kind>/<key>/<child-path>` address emit already accepts) resolves clean, matching emit's own validation.
notes: Field report (cascade composed-spec adoption, engine 0.0.15, observed 2026-08-10, inbox): reproduced with the embedded kind's render hook removed so the projection carries real member.domain fences; emit resolves the address (and refuses a bogus key) but check's graph.route reports it dangling. scoped at f240dc35

summary: SDK-synthesized tap hooks run bare `temper tap` (cwd default "."), so a hook firing from a subdirectory strands its record outside the anchored primary-checkout log

edit.description: TAP_COMMAND (~747) is the literal string "temper tap" with no path argument, so every synthesized tap hook runs with `temper tap`'s cwd default (`.`, src/main.rs `Tap { path }`). Claude Code documents hook cwd as following Claude itself (worktree root after entering one, the new directory after a `cd`), but `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` as staying at the main checkout regardless [code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, retrieved 2026-08-26]. Anchor TAP_COMMAND at `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` (e.g. `temper tap "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"`) so a subdir-cwd hook fire still resolves the primary checkout's log — closing what the 0.0.15 worktree hoist (src/tap.rs::log_path) only half-closed (it only sees a `.git` file at cwd itself).
Hook-registration assertions (~1620-1690) pin the literal `command` field for a synthesized tap hook — update to the anchored command string.
The acceptance test (~607-650) asserting the emitted `command` is literally "temper tap" — update to the anchored form.

tests.asserts: a synthesized tap hook's command field carries the ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} anchor
the projected hook registration's command literal is the anchored form

acceptance: temper install's emitted .claude/settings.json tap hook command fields carry the ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} anchor; sdk/test/emit.test.ts and tests/emit.rs assert the new literal.
notes: Field report (dtmd-temper.md #1, adversarial pass 2026-08-26, inbox): the binary-side root-walk-up (tap.rs resolving upward from an arbitrary cwd) is deliberately declined here as unneeded defense-in-depth — the SDK anchor alone closes both the cwd and worktree-loss halves at the wiring level. scoped at f240dc35

summary: encode the ruled tap record v2: repo-relative identity (raw path demoted to a debug field) plus an ISO-8601 UTC ts, fixing an InstructionsLoaded reader join that has never once succeeded

edit.description: TAP_RECORD_VERSION (21) bumps to 2; TapRecord (102) relativizes `identity` against the same primary-checkout anchor log_path already resolves (demoting the raw absolute path Claude Code sends to a secondary debug field, never dropped) and gains an ISO-8601 UTC `ts`. `append` is the natural site — it already resolves the anchor via log_path before every write.

field()'s join (~55-67) and the requirement-grain tally (~164-174) compare record.identity against member_index's bare member ids by exact string; a repo-relative path never equals a member id. Normalize repo-relative identity to a member id before the join, reusing the lock's own per-member source paths (drift::emit_owned_targets already builds exactly this projection-path-to-member map for the guard) rather than inventing a second one.
Writer unit tests for the version bump, repo-relative identity, the debug raw-path field, and the new ts; an older v1 record must still read and tolerate out loud.

tap_record() helper (~407) and the field-strand suite construct v1-shaped records by absolute-path identity; update to the v2 shape and add the regression this ships to fix — an InstructionsLoaded record naming a real rule now joins (today `temper explain rust` reports zero joins against 31 real records in this repo's own log).

tests.asserts: a v2 record round-trips repo-relative identity, raw debug path, and ts; a v1 record still reads, tolerated and counted
an InstructionsLoaded record naming a real rule joins to that member in the field strand

acceptance: temper explain rust's field strand reports a nonzero join against this repo's own recorded InstructionsLoaded events (today: zero of 31); an older v1 record in the log still reads, tolerated and counted out loud.
notes: Encodes John's 2026-08-26 session recommendation (commit f240dc35, inbox): holds pipeline.md's bespoke-parsed/versioned-in-lockstep category rather than opening the log as a consumable API; scope and canonical-for-external-parsers stay declined per that ruling. scoped at f240dc35

summary: InstructionsLoaded's tap hook registers only under path_glob_match, so an always-on member never gets recorded — contradicting this repo's own context-arrives requirement

edit.description: TELEMETRY_EVENT_HOOKS['InstructionsLoaded'] (~1620) hard-codes matcher: 'path_glob_match', so the synthesized settings.json hook fires for only one of Claude Code's five documented load_reason values (session_start, nested_traversal, path_glob_match, include, compact — code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, retrieved 2026-08-26). Widen to register the remaining reasons — additional per-reason rows or a wildcard matcher — so an always-on member (which loads under session_start) can be recorded at all.
The synthesized InstructionsLoaded hook's matcher assertions (~1620-1690) pin the single path_glob_match value; extend/update for the widened registration.

tests.asserts: the synthesized InstructionsLoaded hook registers for session_start (and the other documented load_reason values), not path_glob_match alone

acceptance: This repo's own context-arrives requirement (.temper/harness.ts, verifier: telemetry(["InstructionsLoaded", "SkillInvoked"])) becomes verifiable in principle — an always-on member's session_start load now registers a tap hook that can fire, where today the wiring structurally excludes it.
notes: Field report (dtmd-temper.md #3, adversarially strengthened 2026-08-26, inbox): this harness's own always-on members load under session_start, which path_glob_match-only matching can never record — an on-contract self-contradiction. Blocked on CWD-ANCHOR only for its shared sdk/test/emit.test.ts edit; recommend shipping alongside/after TAP-RECORD-SCHEMA-V2 so new records actually join (non-blocking). scoped at f240dc35

summary: two fields-only kinds declaring the same collectionAddress are accepted silently; check unions their selections and cross-applies contracts instead of refusing the collision

edit.description: governs_collision_diagnostics (~303-341) explicitly excludes any kind carrying a collection_address, its own doc comment naming the gap: 'two manifest kinds contending for one collection address is a distinct, out-of-scope question.' Add a sibling collection_address_collision_diagnostics keyed on (manifest, key_path) from CollectionAddressRow, mirroring the governs-glob collision shape and rule-id convention (kind.collection-address-collision).
Wire the new diagnostic beside the existing governs_collision_diagnostics call (~205).

Regression mirroring the report's original 0.0.14 repro: declare a second fields-only kind at settings.json/hooks.<Event> (the built-in hook's own address) and assert check refuses the collision loud, rather than unioning both kinds' selections and cross-applying contracts.

tests.asserts: two kinds declared at the same collectionAddress trip a named admissibility error, naming both kinds, instead of unioned/cross-applied selections

acceptance: A corpus declaring two kinds at the same collectionAddress fails admissibility with a kind.collection-address-collision finding naming both kinds; a clean corpus is unaffected.
notes: Field report (dtmd-temper.md #5, adversarial pass 2026-08-26, inbox): the original 0.0.14 repro no longer reproduces on current temper (currency caveat the report itself raises) — confirm-and-regress, not a live crash; paired with #4 as evidence the address/kind model wants tests at this level. scoped at f240dc35

summary: coverage.checked's per-kind member count is file-discovery only, so every embedded-locus kind prints (0) even when it governs hundreds of nested members, reading as dead

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

edit.description: The summary line (~62-75) renders member_counts verbatim as `kind (count)`; member_counts (src/gate.rs:179,254) only tallies discovered files, never nested/embedded members. Thread the lock's nested_member rows (Declarations::nested_members, already read into `committed` at src/gate.rs:66) grouped by child kind, and render an embedded kind's line as `directive (36 embedded)` beside a file kind's `skill (16)` — the filer's stated preference; omitting embedded kinds from the line is the named fallback.
The coverage_note::check call (~477-484) gains the nested-member counts to pass through.
Regression: a lock with nested_member rows against an embedded kind renders that kind's count as nonzero (embedded-marked), not (0).

tests.asserts: an embedded-locus kind carrying nested_member rows renders a nonzero, embedded-marked count in the coverage.checked summary

acceptance: coverage.checked's summary line for an embedded-locus kind carrying nested members states a nonzero count (or the named fallback of omitting it), never a bare misleading (0).
notes: Field report (dtmd-temper.md #4, engine 0.0.15, inbox): the engine evaluates embedded members correctly (extent/max_len/required decide per rendered member) — this is report legibility only. 269 declaration.nested_member rows across 9 embedded kinds in this repo's own lock, every one printing (0) today.
